sources.title: Enumerating number fields
sources.edition: Annals of Mathematics 192 (2020), no. 2, 487–497, version of record
readSections: Theorems 1–2, pp. 487–488, and introductory conventions through p. 489
Proposition 1 and its complete argument, §2, pp. 489–490
Construction and proof of Proposition 2, §3, pp. 491–495
Parameter estimates and counting proof, §4, pp. 495–496; references pp. 496–497

nodes.title: Weighted canonical measure
nodes.statement: On the existing mixed space R^r₁ × C^r₂ use the positive definite real pairing g(x,y)=Σ_real x_i y_i+2 Re(Σ_complex x_j conjugate(y_j)). Its Euclidean Haar measure mu_can is 2^r₂ times standard product volume. The house body B={max(|real coordinates|,|complex coordinates|)≤1} has mu_can-volume 2^r₁(2π)^r₂≥2^n. The house gauge is not the norm from g.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
proofSteps: Scale both real coordinates of each complex factor by sqrt(2). This is an isometry from g to the standard Euclidean metric and has real determinant 2^r₂.
Use change of variables for Haar volume. The sup body is a product of intervals and complex disks, giving the stated volume.
Identify its gauge on embedded K with the built house, since conjugate embeddings have equal modulus.
acceptance: Canonical volume and the house gauge are tracked separately in both Minkowski applications.

sources.locator: §2, p. 489, canonical pairing and measure
sources.match: The source weights complex coordinates twice in the real pairing; this target makes the comparison with the built product volume explicit.

uses.how: Converts the built product-volume covolume to the normalization of the short-integer argument.
The body-volume lower bound cancels the 2^n factor in second Minkowski.

nodes.title: Canonical discriminant covolume
nodes.statement: The mixed-embedding lattice of O_K has canonical covolume sqrt(|disc K|)=delta^(n/2). If beta is an actual integral basis and A has rows indexed by embeddings and columns beta, its canonical Gram determinant is |det A|²=|disc K|.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
proofSteps: Take the existing product-volume identity 2^(−r₂) sqrt(|disc K|) on the existing lattice.
Apply the measure-scaling identity to the same fundamental domain, cancelling 2^r₂.

For the integral-basis matrix use the embedding-determinant discriminant identity and conjugation to obtain |det A|². Nonzero integer discriminant implies |disc K|≥1, and positive-real-power laws give the delta formula.
acceptance: For Q(i), product covolume is 1 and canonical covolume is 2, whose square is |−4|.
A short rational basis cannot replace beta in this discriminant formula.

sources.locator: §2, p. 490, before the first successive-minima application
sources.match: The arithmetic volume is the square root of the absolute field discriminant with the weighted canonical measure.

nodes.title: More than half a degree of short integers
nodes.statement: There exist Q-linearly independent omega_1,…,omega_n∈O_K with nondecreasing houses and product of houses at most delta^(n/2). For m=floor(n/2)+1, all omega_i with i≤m have house at most delta. The family need not be an integral basis.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
proofSteps: Apply the imported second-Minkowski upper product inequality and attaining independent witnesses to the closed house body with canonical volume at least 2^n.
Sort the witnesses by gauge, using the built house lower bound 1 on every nonzero algebraic integer.
Apply the imported ordered-product root bound: house(omega_i)≤delta^(n/(2(n+1−i))). For i≤m, n≤2(n+1−i) and delta≥1 give the result.
Real independence of mixed images implies Q independence; no assertion about the integral span follows.
acceptance: The exact m has 2m>n; choosing only floor(n/2) witnesses is insufficient.

sources.locator: §2, p. 490, first Minkowski application and the choice of m
sources.match: The first m witnesses are small enough for the field-multiplication argument, including the even-degree boundary.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.halfSmallIntegers_house

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.halfSmallIntegers_product

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.halfSmallIntegers_house_eq_gauge

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.half_degree_one

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.half_even_degree

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.half_odd_degree

uses.how: The strict inequality 2m>n is the dimension input.
Products of the first m elements have house at most delta².

nodes.title: Products span the field
nodes.statement: For a finite field extension K/k of degree n and k-subspace V, if 2 dim_k V>n then span_k{ab:a,b∈V}=K. Neither separability nor normality is required.
hypotheses: K/k is a finite extension of fields.
V≤K and 2 dim_k V>[K:k].
proofSteps: If the product span is proper, choose a nonzero k-linear functional f vanishing on it.
The map a↦(b↦f(ab)) from K to its dual is injective: for a≠0 choose c with f(c)≠0 and test b=a^(−1)c.
The image of V is an m-dimensional subspace of the annihilator of V, of dimension n−m. This forces 2m≤n and contradicts the hypothesis.
acceptance: At equality the assertion fails: V=Q in a quadratic field has 2dim V=n but product span Q.
A finite algebra with zero divisors is not substituted for a field.

sources.locator: §2, p. 490, product-span argument before Proposition 1
sources.match: The source uses multiplication to improve bounds from a large short subspace to a full short independent family.

nodes.title: Independent delta-squared-short integers
nodes.statement: For every number field K there exist alpha_1,…,alpha_n∈O_K whose images form a Q-basis of K and satisfy house(alpha_i)≤delta² for all i. In particular they are Z-linearly independent, with no claim that their Z-span is O_K.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
proofSteps: Take the m small integers and apply product-span to their Q-span.
Select n independent products omega_i omega_j from the finite spanning set. They are integral.
For every embedding the modulus of each product is at most delta²; apply the built house/embedding comparison.
acceptance: The existence includes Q, with alpha_1=1.
Every later field-discriminant computation uses a separate genuine integral basis.

sources.locator: Proposition 1 and proof, §2, p. 490
sources.match: The proposition supplies independent short integral elements, which are a rational basis and may have a nontrivial integral index.

nodes.title: Integral generators from a short rational basis
nodes.statement: Given an integral Q-basis alpha_i, define kappa_j(u)=Σ_i u_ij alpha_i for u∈Z^(n×r). Its conjugate configuration is P_tau(u)=(tau(kappa_j(u)))_j. Extending u to C makes u↦P(u) a C-linear equivalence on C^(n×r), with each column transformed by the invertible embedding matrix of alpha. For 0≤u_ij≤D and house(alpha_i)≤delta², house(kappa_j)≤nD delta².
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1; alpha is an integral rational basis, not necessarily an integral basis.
D≥0 is an integer.
proofSteps: Define kappa by the finite integer linear combinations in O_K; the embedding formula follows by additivity.
The embedding matrix of a rational basis has nonzero determinant: use nonzero basis discriminant and its square embedding-determinant formula. Apply its inverse separately in each of the r columns.
Bound each conjugate by the triangle inequality and n summands at most D delta².
acceptance: The inverse matrix is used over C; integrality of its entries is never asserted.

sources.locator: §3, pp. 491–492, before the bounded integer parameter choice
sources.match: The basis coordinates range over a full affine parameter space, so a generic minor stays nonzero after pullback.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameterizedGenerators
api.statement: For alpha and u return the tuple kappa∈O_K^r with the stated finite-sum formula.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameterizedGenerators_embedding
api.statement: tau(kappa_j)=Σ_i (u_ij:C) tau(alpha_i).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameterConfigurationEquiv
api.statement: The complex-linear parameter-to-conjugate-configuration map is invertible for a rational basis alpha.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameterizedGenerators_house_le
api.statement: Parameters in [0,D] give house(kappa_j)≤nD delta².

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameterizedGenerators_reindex
api.statement: Reindexing alpha and the first index of u together leaves kappa unchanged; an integral basis change acts by the inverse coefficient change.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameter_rat
tests.statement: For K=Q, alpha=(1), and u_11=3, kappa_1=3.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameter_zero
tests.statement: The zero parameter matrix gives the zero tuple, whose first jets need not have the required rank.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameter_nonbasis

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.parameter_singular_family
tests.statement: Repeated alpha entries are rejected by the rational-basis hypothesis; their configuration map is singular.

uses.how: Invertibility proves nonzeroness of the pulled-back interpolation minor.
The explicit bound nD delta² controls monomial evaluation.

nodes.title: Bounded arithmetic first-jet parameters
nodes.statement: Under r≥1,d≥5,M≥n(r+1), there is u∈{0,…,D}^(n×r), D=dn(r+1), such that the degree-d first-jet map at the n conjugate points of kappa(u) is surjective over C. These points are distinct and house(kappa_j)≤n²d(r+1)delta².
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
proofSteps: Import a nonzero n(r+1)-column maximal minor on the generic affine configuration space and its total-degree bound D.
Pull it back by the complex-linear equivalence of parameterized-generators. The pullback is nonzero; linear substitution preserves the total-degree bound D, hence bounds every variable degree by D.

Apply the built grid-vanishing lemma over C to the coordinate sets {0,…,D}, each of cardinality D+1. This allows the complex embedding coefficients; the integer-coefficient-only parameter export is not misapplied.
The resulting integer tuple has nonzero minor, so first jets are onto and repeated conjugate points are impossible. Insert D into the house bound.
acceptance: The grid uses D+1 choices per parameter; D choices do not follow from a degree≤D bound.
For seven collinear points in A² at d=5, distinctness and the dimension inequality alone do not imply full jets.

sources.locator: §3, pp. 491–492, maximal minor and integer parameter grid
sources.match: A nonzero pulled-back minor admits bounded integer specialization; the generic statement alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: Descent of value evaluation
nodes.statement: For the chosen tuple kappa, evaluation V_Q(r,d)→K is Q-linearly surjective, and evaluation Q[x_1,…,x_r]→K is a surjective Q-algebra map. Hence Q[kappa_1,…,kappa_r]=K. The integral bounded-degree evaluation into O_K is not asserted surjective.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
The conjugate first-jet map of kappa is onto.
proofSteps: Project the full first-jet map onto its n value rows; this is onto C^n.

In a rational basis of K the degree-bounded evaluation is a rational n×M matrix B_Q. After extension to C, multiplication by the invertible embedding matrix identifies it with the value matrix, which has rank n.
A rational matrix has the same rank after extension to C, by nonvanishing of its minors. Thus the rational bounded evaluation is onto. The full algebra map contains this image and is also onto.
acceptance: Tensoring an integral image with Q can be onto while its integral index remains greater than one.
The morphism Spec K→A^r_Q comes from the actual evaluation map.

sources.locator: §3, p. 492, closed immersion induced by the kappa tuple
sources.match: Value surjectivity descends from the complex conjugate configuration and supplies the field-valued closed point.

nodes.title: The integral relation lattice
nodes.statement: Let V_Z(r,d)=MvPolynomial.restrictTotalDegree(Fin r,Z,d) and ev_Z:V_Z→O_K be evaluation at the chosen integral tuple kappa. Define L=ker(ev_Z) in the existing monomial coordinate lattice Z^M. Equip its real span with the coefficient Euclidean metric imported from GI.0. Then L is saturated, rank_Z L=ell=M−n, and its complex span is precisely the kernel of value evaluation at all conjugates.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
The tuple has degree-d rational value evaluation onto K.
proofSteps: Restrict native algebra evaluation to the existing bounded polynomial submodule; use the supplied coefficient-coordinate equivalence to regard its kernel as an integer submodule of Z^M.
Its quotient is the integral evaluation image in the torsion-free group O_K, so L is saturated. Use a genuine integral basis to express evaluation by an integer matrix B of rational rank n.
Integer null vectors span the rational kernel by clearing denominators in a rational nullspace basis. Extension of this matrix kernel to R or C then gives rank M−n and the stated kernel comparison.
Transport the Euclidean metric from the monomial coordinates; do not use a polynomial sup norm.
acceptance: L is considered as a full lattice in its ell-dimensional real span, not in all R^M.

sources.locator: §3, p. 493, lattice L and coefficient inner product
sources.match: The kernel is the arithmetic relation lattice in native bounded-degree polynomials, with its intrinsic coefficient metric.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice
api.statement: L is the kernel of bounded-degree integral evaluation.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.mem_relationLattice

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_rank

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_saturated
api.statement: If a≠0 is integral and af∈L then f∈L.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_complexSpan
api.statement: In coefficient coordinates L⊗C is the kernel of conjugate value evaluation.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_degree_mono
api.statement: For d≤e, the native degree inclusion maps L_d into L_e compatibly with coefficients and evaluation.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relations_zero_tuple
tests.statement: For one variable, kappa=0 and d=2, the kernel has integral basis X,X²; the constant coefficient must vanish.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relations_degree_zero
tests.statement: For d=0, constant evaluation Z→O_K is injective, so the kernel is zero; the full-value-rank hypothesis then holds only for n=1.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relations_square_root
tests.statement: For kappa=sqrt(2), r=1,d=3, the kernel is spanned over Z by X²−2 and X³−2X, with rank 2=(d+1)−n.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relations_nonintegral_tuple
tests.statement: The tuple 1/2∈Q does not define this map into O_Q=Z and is excluded.

uses.how: Saturation identifies the primitive integral orthogonal.
The real lattice gives short integral equations; its complex span is the entire value kernel.

nodes.title: Transpose image and its integral index
nodes.statement: Let Lperp=(span_R L)^perp∩Z^M. Transpose integral evaluation gives an injection ev_Z^*:Hom_Z(O_K,Z)→Z^M, lambda↦(lambda(kappa^alpha))_alpha, with image S⊆Lperp of finite index q≥1. Both have rank n and covol(S)=q covol(Lperp). More precisely q=[O_K:im(ev_Z)]. Thus covol(L)=covol(Lperp)≤covol(S), by primitive orthogonal covolume in the standard unimodular coefficient lattice.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
The integral evaluation image has rank n.
proofSteps: A functional on O_K annihilates the kernel after composition with evaluation; therefore its coordinate row lies in the integral orthogonal. Rational surjectivity makes the transpose injective and gives rank n.

The saturation and kernel comparison identify Lperp with the full dual of the evaluation image, using the perfect coordinate pairing on Z^M. Restriction from O_K-dual to image-dual has index [O_K:image].
Apply the built intrinsic relative-index formula to S⊆Lperp in their common real span.
Apply the imported primitive orthogonal-covolume theorem to saturated L in standard self-dual Z^M.
acceptance: The direction of the inequality is covol(L)≤covol(S), and q is never silently set to 1.

sources.locator: §3, p. 493, integral orthogonal and transpose evaluation
sources.match: The source uses a finite-index sublattice to bound the covolume. Equality with the whole orthogonal is not needed.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dualEvaluation
api.statement: Send lambda∈Hom_Z(O_K,Z) to its values on the evaluated bounded monomials.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dualEvaluation_apply
api.statement: The alpha coordinate is lambda(kappa^alpha).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dualEvaluation_injective

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dualEvaluation_image_le_orthogonal
api.statement: S is contained in Lperp and has the same rank n.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dualEvaluation_index
api.statement: [Lperp:S]=[O_K:im(ev_Z)] and covol(S) is this index times covol(Lperp).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dualEvaluation_basis_change
api.statement: Changing the integral basis of O_K changes the generators of S by a unimodular matrix and leaves S and its covolume unchanged.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dual_index_two

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dual_full_image
tests.statement: For kappa=sqrt(2) in Q(sqrt(2)), d≥1, evaluation contains the integral basis 1,sqrt(2); hence S=Lperp.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.dual_zero_kernel
tests.statement: For the abstract integer map Z→Z, z↦2z, the kernel is zero, its integral orthogonal is Z, and the dual image is 2Z, of covolume 2 rather than 1.

uses.how: The rows of the integral evaluation matrix generate S.
Its larger covolume is an upper bound for the relation-lattice covolume.

nodes.title: The Gram–discriminant identity
nodes.statement: Choose an actual integral basis beta of O_K. Let A_tau,i=tau(beta_i), B_i,alpha the integer beta-coordinates of kappa^alpha, and V_tau,alpha=tau(kappa^alpha), so V=AB. Then B is real/integer, S=B^t Z^n, covol(S)²=det(BB^t), and det(BB^t)=det(V conjugate(V)^t)/|disc K|. Both determinants in the ratio are nonnegative reals; the denominator is nonzero.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
The matrices have shapes A:n×n, B:n×M, V:n×M; B has row rank n.
proofSteps: The basis-coordinate identity gives V=AB. Consequently V V*=A(BB^t)A*, where * is conjugate transpose and B is real.
Take determinants and use det(A)conjugate(det(A))=|disc K| for the genuine integral basis.
The rows of B are an integral basis of S because the transpose is injective. Apply the intrinsic Gram-volume formula, or an orthonormal coordinate determinant, in the row span.
acceptance: Use V conjugate(V)^t, not VV^t, in the positive Hermitian Gram matrix.
The short alpha family is not used as beta.

sources.locator: §3, pp. 493–494, evaluation matrix and determinant computation
sources.match: The determinant comparison retains the absolute field-discriminant denominator and the complex conjugation.

nodes.title: Height of monomial values
nodes.statement: Put C0=n²d(r+1)delta², H0=C0^d and G=M H0². Every entry of V has modulus at most H0. Thus every diagonal entry of the Hermitian Gram matrix V V* is at most G. These inequalities include the degree-zero monomial because C0≥1.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
The chosen tuple has house(kappa_j)≤C0.
proofSteps: For each bounded exponent alpha, the evaluated monomial has modulus at most C0^(sum alpha)≤C0^d.
Each diagonal Gram entry is a sum of M squared moduli.
Separate the constant monomial and note C0≥1; there are M, not (d+1)^r, monomials.
acceptance: H0=[n²d(r+1)]^d delta^(2d); G=M[n²d(r+1)]^(2d)delta^(4d).
The constant monomial contributes 1.

sources.locator: §3, pp. 493–494, entrywise and diagonal Gram estimates
sources.match: The evaluation bound fixes both the n²d(r+1) factor and the 2d power of the root discriminant.

nodes.title: Covolume of arithmetic relations
nodes.statement: For G=M[n²d(r+1)]^(2d)delta^(4d), the intrinsic relation covolume satisfies covol(L)≤G^(n/2)/sqrt(|disc K|)≤G^(n/2). The ambient standard monomial lattice is unimodular; all covolumes of L use its ell-dimensional real span.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
proofSteps: Use primitive orthogonal equality and S⊆Lperp to bound covol(L) by covol(S).
Use the Gram–discriminant identity and imported Hermitian Hadamard inequality to bound det(VV*) by G^n.
Take positive square roots, retaining sqrt(|disc K|) in the denominator; use |disc K|≥1 only for the second inequality.
acceptance: The coefficient space uses its unweighted monomial Euclidean measure, independently of the earlier canonical measure.

sources.locator: §3, p. 494, covolume bound before second Minkowski
sources.match: This is the arithmetic specialization of the generic Gram bound and the finite-index comparison.

nodes.title: Independent short relation witnesses
nodes.statement: There exist ell linearly independent integral relations E_1,…,E_ell∈L, sorted by coefficient Euclidean norm, with each norm≥1 and product at most ell^(ell/2) covol(L)≤ell^(ell/2)G^(n/2). They form a real basis of span_R L but need not be an integral basis of L.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
proofSteps: Use the intrinsic ell-dimensional coefficient Euclidean space and the closed unit ball. Its volume is at least 2^ell ell^(−ell/2), by the supplied inscribed-cube inequality.
Apply second Minkowski and its attaining independent witnesses to L in that space, then sort them.
Each nonzero integer coefficient vector has norm at least one. Substitute the relation-covolume upper bound.
acceptance: No step uses the two different archimedean and coefficient measures interchangeably.

sources.locator: §3, p. 494, second Minkowski application to equations
sources.match: The second independent family lives in the relation space and uses the coefficient Euclidean ball.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.exists_shortRelations
api.statement: Return ell independent integral equations, their sorted norms, and the product bound.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.shortRelations_mem
api.statement: Every witness vanishes at kappa and has total degree at most d.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.shortRelations_independent

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.shortRelations_norm_lower

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.shortRelations_coefficient_le

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relation_norm_single

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relation_norm_integral

uses.how: Sorted norms and the product bound control the retained initial segment.
The full ell-family spans the relation kernel over C.

nodes.title: Dropping exactly n minus one relations
nodes.statement: Keep k=ell+1−n of the sorted relations, discarding exactly n−1. The number k is positive, and every retained relation has Euclidean norm and hence each coefficient modulus at most ell^(ell/(2n)) sqrt(G). Their complex span W has codimension n−1 in L_C.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
E_1,…,E_ell are the sorted independent witnesses.
proofSteps: For one-based i≤k, ell+1−i≥n. Apply the imported ordered-product root bound to the witness norms.
The product bound gives norm(E_i)≤[ell^(ell/2)G^(n/2)]^(1/n)=ell^(ell/(2n))sqrt(G), since both factors are at least one.
Full independence gives dim W=k, so its codimension in the ell-dimensional relation space is n−1. The rank inequality ell≥nr gives k≥n(r−1)+1≥1.
acceptance: Keeping ell−n instead loses the strict codimension inequality needed for a full gradient block.
The output bound is ell^(ell/(2n))sqrt(M)[n²d(r+1)]^d delta^(2d).

sources.locator: §3, p. 494, removing the last n−1 equations
sources.match: The truncation trades a small codimension for a uniform coefficient bound.

nodes.title: All conjugate gradient blocks are onto
nodes.statement: The derivative map L_C→Π_tau C^r, f↦((partial_j f)(P_tau))_(tau,j), is surjective. Here L_C is the complex span of the integral relation lattice, equal to the full degree-d value kernel; no reduction to the retained subspace is made yet.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
The chosen conjugate first-jet map is surjective.
proofSteps: Use the relation-lattice scalar-extension identification with the value kernel.
Apply the imported first-jet kernel splitting theorem: surjectivity of values and first derivatives together gives derivative surjectivity on the value kernel.
Record all n blocks at once, so their independent codimension contributions can be used after truncation.
acceptance: Value surjectivity by itself does not imply this derivative statement.

sources.locator: §3, p. 494, well-poisedness and the cotangent-space argument
sources.match: First jets control the derivative map on the complete relation kernel.

nodes.title: A retained family spans one gradient block
nodes.statement: For W spanned by the retained k relations, at least one embedding tau has surjective gradient map W→C^r. Equivalently the k×r gradient matrix has rank r at that conjugate. The strict codimension n−1<n is essential.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
W has codimension n−1 in L_C.
The full gradient map L_C→Π_tau C^r is onto.
proofSteps: Let Y be the image of W in the product of gradient blocks. A surjection sends a subspace to a subspace of codimension at most its original codimension, so codim(Y)≤n−1.
If all block projections of Y were proper, choose a nonzero functional on each C^r vanishing on that projected image.
The n functionals on disjoint blocks are independent and vanish on Y, forcing codim(Y)≥n, a contradiction.
acceptance: At codimension n this can fail: in (C^r)^n, the product of n fixed hyperplanes has codimension n and every block is proper.

sources.locator: §3, p. 494, existence of a full-rank embedding block
sources.match: The paper’s dimension step is made explicit as an independent-block annihilator argument.

nodes.title: One minor at every conjugate
nodes.statement: Choose r retained equations whose r×r gradient minor is nonzero at the full-rank embedding. Their Jacobian determinant evaluated at kappa is a nonzero element of K; hence that same chosen minor is nonzero under every embedding K→C. The equations retain degree≤d and the truncation coefficient bound.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
proofSteps: Full rank supplies r distinct retained rows and a nonzero determinant at one embedding.
Form J(kappa)=det((partial_j E_i)(kappa)) in K. Evaluation and determinants commute with field embeddings.
Nonzero image implies J(kappa)≠0; every field embedding is injective, so all its conjugates are nonzero. This does not assume K/Q normal.
acceptance: A tuple in a nonnormal cubic field is still covered by injectivity of its embeddings.
All selected equations are integral relations, not merely complex linear combinations.

sources.locator: §3, pp. 494–495, the minor preceding Proposition 2
sources.match: A single rationally defined determinant works at every conjugate point; rows are not chosen separately for each point.

nodes.title: The arithmetic component map
nodes.statement: For the selected integer equations E and J=det(partial_j E_i), form A_E=(Q[x_1,…,x_r]/(E_1,…,E_r)) localized away from the class of J. Use the supplier’s existing Jacobian-open algebra. Since E_i(kappa)=0 and J(kappa)≠0, polynomial evaluation extends uniquely to a surjective Q-algebra map phi:A_E→K. It exhibits Spec K as one open and closed irreducible component of Spec A_E. A_E itself may have other field factors.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
E is the selected r-tuple from common-jacobian-minor.
proofSteps: Factor native Q-polynomial evaluation through the ideal generated by the E_i using their vanishing.
Send the inverted Jacobian to J(kappa)^(−1); localization’s universal property gives the actual map, compatible with evaluation. Its image contains the surjective polynomial evaluation image.
Invoke SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/jacobian-etale-algebra for finite etaleness and the decomposition compatible with the surjection. Do not reprove its generic presentation theorem.
acceptance: The universal property fixes phi, not merely an abstract isomorphic field somewhere in A_E.

sources.locator: Proposition 2, p. 495, and §3 pp. 492, 494
sources.match: The nonvanishing minor supplies the localization point; the quotient field is a component of the finite-etale algebra.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.jacobianAt
api.statement: For an ordered r-tuple E of integer polynomials and a tuple kappa in a commutative ring R, evaluate the determinant of the r by r matrix of native partial derivatives. This equals evaluation of the polynomial Jacobian determinant.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.jacobianAt_map
api.statement: For a ring homomorphism f:R→S, f(jacobianAt(kappa,E))=jacobianAt(f∘kappa,E); hence injective field embeddings preserve its nonvanishing.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.componentEvaluation
api.statement: Extend the specific evaluation map to A_E by inverting J(kappa).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.componentEvaluation_polynomial
api.statement: On the image of f∈Q[x], phi equals f(kappa).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.componentEvaluation_inverseJacobian
api.statement: The image of the inverse Jacobian is J(kappa)^(−1).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.componentEvaluation_unique
api.statement: It is the unique algebra map agreeing with polynomial evaluation.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.componentEvaluation_surjective
api.statement: phi is onto K because bounded-degree rational values already span K.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.componentEvaluation_factor
api.statement: The supplier’s finite-product equivalence can be chosen with phi the projection to its K factor.

tests.statement: For E=X² at kappa=0, J(kappa)=0 and the Jacobian-open algebra is zero; no map of this construction onto Q exists.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.jacobian_empty

uses.how: Combines the arithmetic bounds with the correct geometric component statement.
Several field components per model are permitted and must be counted.

nodes.title: Explicit small field models
nodes.statement: For every number field K and integers r≥1,d≥5 with M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), there are integral kappa_1,…,kappa_r and integer polynomials E_1,…,E_r of total degree≤d, all coefficients of modulus at most B(n,r,d,delta)=ell^(ell/(2n))sqrt(M)[n²d(r+1)]^d delta^(2d), where ell=M−n. They vanish at kappa, generate K as a Q-algebra by evaluation, and have J(kappa)≠0. Thus Spec K is an open and closed irreducible component of the finite-etale Jacobian-open model A_E.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
r≥1, d≥5, M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), ell=M−n≥nr>0.
proofSteps: Use bounded arithmetic first jets and the descended value evaluation to construct the relation lattice.
Apply the covolume estimate, short independent witnesses, truncation and the full-block argument.
Retain the same selected r equations and substitute G into the coefficient bound. Apply the arithmetic component map.
acceptance: The theorem allows n=1 and r=1 when the other inequalities hold.
It never asserts that r short equations generate the full relation ideal or that the whole zero locus is zero-dimensional.

sources.locator: Proposition 2, §3, p. 495
sources.match: The explicit polynomial coefficient bound and the field-as-component conclusion are the arithmetic model theorem.

nodes.title: The least central-binomial rank
nodes.statement: For each n≥1 define r(n) as the least positive integer r with n(r+1)≤choose(2r,r). Write F_r=choose(2r,r)/(r+1). Then F_(r+1)/F_r=2(2r+1)/(r+2)<4, r(n) exists, and n(r+1)≤choose(2r,r)≤4n(r+1). Eventually r≥5 and r≤3 log n, for natural logarithm.
hypotheses: n≥1 is an integer.
The estimate r≤3 log n is eventual, not asserted at n=1.
proofSteps: The central binomial coefficient is at least 2^r, so F_r grows without bound; for example 2^r/(r+1) suffices. Thus least positive r exists.
For r>1, minimality gives F_(r−1)<n and the exact consecutive ratio gives F_r<4n. At r=1 the bound holds directly.

Since F_4=14 and F_r is increasing, n>14 forces r≥5. To get r≤3 log n eventually, use choose(2r,r)≥4^r/(2r+1), as the largest summand in the binomial sum 4^r. For r=floor(3 log n) the ratio 4^r/((2r+1)(r+1)n) tends to infinity, so F_r≥n for large n.
acceptance: The chosen d=r is inserted into Proposition 2 only in the eventual r≥5 range.

sources.locator: §4, p. 495, equation (1) and the parameter choice
sources.match: The normalized central binomial coefficient grows exponentially while its consecutive ratio is less than four.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.centralBinomialRank
api.statement: Return the least positive admissible r for n≥1.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.centralBinomialRank_spec
api.statement: r>0, n(r+1)≤choose(2r,r), and each positive s<r is inadmissible.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.centralBinomialRank_size
api.statement: The monomial count lies between n(r+1) and 4n(r+1).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.centralBinomialRank_log
api.statement: There exists an absolute n0 such that n≥n0 implies 5≤r≤3 log n.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.centralBinomialRank_mono
api.statement: For 1≤n≤m, r(n)≤r(m).

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.rank_one_two
tests.statement: r(1)=1 and r(2)=2, because choose(2,1)=2 and choose(4,2)=6.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.rank_no_log_at_one
tests.statement: r(1)=1>3 log 1=0, so an all-n logarithmic bound is rejected.

uses.how: Set d=r to get logarithmic equation count, degree and coefficient height.
The same r depends only on n and controls the common finite coefficient box.

nodes.title: Logarithmic small models
nodes.statement: There is one absolute real Q≥3 such that for every number field K of degree n>Q one can take r=d=r(n)≤Q log n and M=choose(2r,r)≤Q n log n in the explicit small-model theorem, with every coefficient at most (n delta)^(Q log n). The resulting Jacobian-open model contains Spec K as an irreducible component.
hypotheses: K is a number field, n=[K:Q]≥1, delta=NumberField.rootDiscr K, and delta≥1.
n is larger than the single absolute threshold Q.
proofSteps: Choose n above the central-binomial threshold and take d=r(n)≥5. We have ell≤M≤4n(r+1)=O(n log n).
Taking logarithms, log(ell^(ell/(2n)))=(ell/(2n))log ell=O((log n)²). Also log(sqrt(M))=O(log n).
For the remaining factors, d log(n²d(r+1))=O((log n)²) and 2d log delta=O(log n log delta). Combine into Q log n (log n+log delta).
Enlarge one absolute Q to dominate every threshold and constant, then exponentiate and apply the explicit model theorem.
acceptance: The r used in counting is a function only of n, not of K or its discriminant.
No numerical value of the absolute constant is claimed.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, p. 487, proved in §4 pp. 495–496
sources.match: A single sufficiently large absolute constant controls the eventual degree range and each bound.

nodes.title: Bounded integer equation systems
nodes.statement: For naturals r,d,C, let Box(r,d,C) be the set of ordered r-tuples E of native integer polynomials in r variables such that totalDegree(E_i)≤d and |coeff_alpha(E_i)|≤C for every i and exponent alpha. In the supplied monomial coordinates this is exactly rM independent integer slots in [−C,C], M=choose(d+r,d). This coefficient-box carrier is separate from any field-isomorphism carrier.
hypotheses: r,d,C≥0 are integers.
All equations have exactly the same variable index Fin r, and the tuple is ordered.
proofSteps: Take the subset of (Z[x_1,…,x_r])^r specified by the degree and coefficient inequalities.
Apply the imported coefficient-coordinate equivalence to the bounded-degree submodule. Coefficients outside the bounded exponent set vanish.
This identifies the set with the product over Fin r×A(r,d) of the finite integer interval [−C,C].
acceptance: Ordering equations counts every possible tuple and only overcounts models.

sources.locator: §4, p. 496, the number of coefficients to be specified
sources.match: The proof’s finite coefficient choices are recorded as an actual subset of the existing polynomial carrier.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.boundedEquationSystems
api.statement: The subset of ordered r-tuples cut out by total degree≤d and absolute coefficient≤C.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.mem_boundedEquationSystems
api.statement: Membership is exactly the degree and coefficient conjunction, including the zero polynomial.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.boundedEquationSystems_coeffEquiv

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.boundedEquationSystems_finite

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.boundedEquationSystems_mono

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.boundedEquationSystems_native

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.box_constants
tests.statement: For d=0 there are r constant equations and (2C+1)^r choices.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.box_zero_height

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.box_total_degree

uses.how: The finite product equivalence gives the exact box cardinality.
These finite ordered systems form the domain of the model-to-component counting relation.

nodes.title: The coefficient-box cardinality
nodes.statement: The finite set Box(r,d,C) has cardinality exactly (2C+1)^(r choose(d+r,d)), for all natural r,d,C. If a real coefficient bound B≥0 is used, put C=floor(B); all integer coefficients with modulus≤B lie in this box.
hypotheses: r,d,C≥0 are integers.
For the floor version B is a nonnegative real number.
proofSteps: Use the coefficient-coordinate product equivalence and the exact count 2C+1 for the integer interval [−C,C].
The number of coordinates is rM by the imported monomial count.
For the real bound, integer absolute values satisfy |a|≤B iff |a|≤floor(B), so rounding does not introduce infinitely many choices.
acceptance: At r=1 this recovers the familiar (2C+1)^(d+1) count for degree≤d integer polynomials.

sources.locator: §4, p. 496, counting r choose(2r,r) coefficients
sources.match: The finite coefficient count is made explicit before estimating its logarithm.

nodes.title: From finite models to field classes
nodes.statement: For r,d≥1 and C≥0, the number of Q-isomorphism classes of fields that occur as residue fields of components of Jacobian-open algebras A_E for E∈Box(r,d,C) is at most (2C+1)^(rM) d^r. The same bound holds after restriction to exact degree n and |disc|≤H. This uses a surjection from pairs (equation tuple, field factor) onto the represented classes, not an injection from fields to tuples.
hypotheses: The isolated-point Bezout bound for arbitrary r is supplied by SF.5: at most d^r isolated geometric points of r equations of total degree≤d over an algebraically closed field, even with positive-dimensional components elsewhere.
Count Q-algebra-isomorphism classes using ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0.
proofSteps: For each E use the imported finite-etale classification of A_E. Its factors give a finite set of residue-field classes; repeated isomorphic factors contribute just one class but can be overcounted.

After base change to Qbar, the number of geometric points is the sum of the factor degrees and is at most d^r by the requested isolated-point inequality. Each factor has positive degree, so its number of factors is also at most d^r.
Form the finite disjoint union of these factor sets over the coefficient box and map each pair to its field-isomorphism class. Its image is precisely the represented set.
Apply the coefficient-box count. Restricting degree or discriminant can only decrease the image size.
acceptance: For (X²−2)(X²−3) one equation represents two distinct quadratic classes, so a one-model-one-field argument fails.
The existing SF.5 isolated-plane statement is not substituted for arbitrary dimension.
No factor n/#Aut(K) appears in the unweighted class count.

sources.locator: §4, p. 496, final isolated-point intersection argument; Theorem 2 p. 488
sources.match: Several fields can occur in one model; intersection degree bounds this multiplicity without imposing properness on the whole intersection.

nodes.title: A cubic-logarithmic discriminant exponent
nodes.statement: There exists an absolute real Q≥3 such that, for all integers n>Q and H≥1, the number N_n(H) of Q-isomorphism classes of number fields of exact degree n and |disc K|≤H satisfies N_n(H)≤n^(Q n (log n)^3) H^(Q (log n)^3). All logarithms are natural; the same Q is uniform in n and H.
hypotheses: Use the ST.0 isomorphism-family carrier, with its degree and absolute field-discriminant height.
n is above the single absolute threshold Q, H is an integer≥1.
proofSteps: Finiteness is inherited from the completed Hermite–Minkowski infrastructure in a fixed Qbar and the isomorphism-family quotient, rather than defining an unsupported finite count.
For each class use the logarithmic model with the same r=d=r(n) and M depending only on n. From delta≤H^(1/n), take the common height B=(n H^(1/n))^(Q0 log n), C=floor(B).
All these classes lie in the image counted by components-to-classes, so N_n(H)≤(2C+1)^(rM) r^r. Since B≥1, 2C+1≤3B.
Use rM=O(n(log n)²). The logarithm of the bound is O(n(log n)^3 log n)+O((log n)^3 log H)+O(log n log log n). Absorb the last term and constants into Q n(log n)^3 log n and Q(log n)^3 log H.
Choose one Q≥3 dominating Q0, every degree threshold and both constants, then exponentiate. H=1 is included by the same bound; the proof never divides by log H.
acceptance: This is an upper bound for exact-degree unweighted isomorphism classes, not a density or an asymptotic equality.
The constant is independent of H; the n=1 case is outside the eventual theorem.

sources.locator: Theorem 2, p. 488, and §4 pp. 495–496
sources.match: The discriminant exponent is O((log n)^3), with an explicit displayed dependence on the field degree.

Upstream status records the roadmap on main. Its generic Jacobian-open target is imported by the exact existing atlas node. The general SF.5 Bezout request is an interface clarification to this owner, not a proposal to rebuild its roadmap.
